title: Incremental cost of conservative legacy-query eviction (temporalio/sdk-rust#1835)
scope: Core-level benchmark: sdk-core lib test with a mocked server and a minimal synthetic language implementation. Not a real-server or real-language-SDK measurement and not a production latency estimate.

environment.vm: QEMU guest, 6 vCPU (CPU implementer 0x61, Apple), 1 thread per core, 7.7 GiB RAM

build.rustflags: none (RUSTFLAGS unset; no [profile.release] override; no build.rustflags)

harness.timed_window: From the mocked poll stream handing the next real workflow task to Core until the mocked server receives that task's completion (s4: the completion carrying RecordMarker).
harness.next_wft_delivery: sticky incremental history (s0-s3); full history (s4, as in W4)
harness.worker: max_cached_workflows=1, otherwise mock defaults; no tracing subscriber
harness.synthetic_lang: a few lines of Rust per activation; not a model of a language SDK's cost
harness.cpu_time: sum of /proc/self/task/*/schedstat on-CPU ns over all threads during the window
harness.rss_growth: VmHWM after the window minus VmRSS at the start (VmHWM reset via clear_refs=5); allocator-dependent, rough

scenarios.s0: normal workflow task, no legacy query
scenarios.s1: legacy query before the signal acknowledgement; its preparation runs no workflow code
scenarios.s2: legacy query after the acknowledgement runs workflow code; next task adds only its own WorkflowTaskStarted (A reuses the run, B evicts and rebuilds)
scenarios.s3sig: as s2, next task carries a new signal (A and B both evict)
scenarios.s3upd: as s2, next task carries an update request (A and B both evict)
scenarios.s4: W4 workload: local-activity result held across an effectful legacy query (A and B both evict); la_delay_ms is a sleep inside each local-activity execution
scenarios.history_shape: cycles x (WFTCompleted, TimerStarted, TimerFired, WFTScheduled, WFTStarted) plus 8 fixed events; s3sig adds one signal event

matrix.s2: cycles 0,18,198,998,1998; 10 rounds x 10 samples (+3 warm-up per process)
matrix.s4: 10 rounds x 10 (+3); with la_delay_ms=20: 6 rounds x 5 (+2)
matrix.verify: every cell above, 3 samples per label, separate processes, before the timed matrix
matrix.interleaving: each round runs every label in a fresh process; label order reverses on odd rounds

discrepancies: The original report listed the build features as envconfig, prometheus, tls-ring. Cargo's artifact record shows default, envconfig, ephemeral-server, prometheus, tls-ring (ephemeral-server enabled by workspace feature unification), identical for U, A and B. Measurements are unaffected.

The original report gave one history byte size per history length (the S2 median). Sizes vary by up to 7.5% between samples of the same cell: TestHistoryBuilder stamps every event with SystemTime::now(), and the protobuf varint length of the timestamp varies. results.json gives min/median/max.

All 672 numeric values printed by the original analysis (timed_summary.md) were recomputed from the raw JSONL; all agree at the printed precision. Re-running analyze.py, scaling.py and verify_summary.py reproduces the saved tables byte-for-byte.

statistics.ci: bootstrap of median difference, 2000 resamples, random.Random(1766) reseeded per comparison, resample A then label, 2.5/97.5 percentiles
statistics.test: two-sided Mann-Whitney U, normal approximation with tie correction

s2_scaling.method: Ordinary least squares over the five S2 points (B median - A median) versus the workflow-task count of the history; log-log slope over the points with >= 20 WFTs; marginal slope between adjacent points. Describes this timer-cycle workload (5 events per WFT) over 2-2,000 WFTs only.
